integrity: Analytic argument and reproducible exact rational checks are provided; bounded computations do not prove infinite assertions.
scientific_limitations: The finite census has one species of abundance B and r species each of abundance one.
Uniform sampling is without replacement and species IDs are observed without error.
The transition theorem assumes n>=3, r>=n-1, B>=2, not arbitrary abundance profiles.
A frequency-count covariance alone does not establish bias or coverage of nonlinear diversity estimators.
Some related full documents were unavailable; independent bibliographic validation remains outstanding.
title: A one-crossing singleton–doubleton covariance law in dominant-species rarefaction
